minutes.headline: Commission will keep funding Marshall Park design but delay the next town-meeting vote about a year
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission spent most of the meeting deciding what to do with remaining ARPA and capital design money for Marshall Park, concluding it will keep funding the design but will not bring the project back to town meeting this November, instead waiting roughly a year given the town's broader financial uncertainty. It also heard a skate park funding/construction update, discussed a capital-planning wish list, and reviewed how little park user fees cover of actual maintenance and school-field rental costs compared with other towns, without changing fees.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of March 26, April 9, April 26, and June 4 with the edits/corrections discussed (name spellings, 'floor' to 'flood')

budget_items.what_was_said: Bids for resurfacing the Wallace tennis/basketball courts were due Monday after the original contractor lost his state-contract status and had to rebid.

The insurance company approved the claim for a vehicle that crashed through the fence and into the toddler play structure at Wallace Park; the structure was removed and mulch replaced as a precaution.
The chair has a list of cultural council grant opportunities, due in September or October, to pass along to Angela, including possible replacements for a vendor who is not returning.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park ARPA and capital design funds
budget_items.what_was_said: About $13,000 in ARPA funds remains and must be used by year end or lost back to the federal government; a separate total of $97,000 remains from capital funds for the design/engineering process.

budget_items.topic: Design draw percentage reached before town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: Members tried to recall what percentage draw on the design contract had been reached before annual town meeting, with figures of 60%, 75%, and 34% all mentioned and not resolved.
The skate park presenter reported the project is roughly 91% funded (later restated around 330-ish), with an overall project total described as about 372, including in-kind donations.
About 98% of contract terms with the builder have been negotiated, with only the bonding structure still outstanding; the goal is a signed contract by Labor Day.
An initial amount, heard as 'the initial 50,' was allocated to start a weeds treatment pilot program; no further capital request will be added until that work begins.
The chair said she is sticking with a request to add $10,000 a year to the parks operating budget, which could help fund smaller maintenance projects.

budget_items.topic: Field maintenance contract vs. actual mowing costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The current mowing contract is written for 17 mowings per season, but actual mowing far exceeds that number, so real costs are higher than the contract price shown.

The current parks fee is $20 per resident participant and $30 per non-resident; youth baseball reported 148 participants this spring for a total of $2,960 to reserve five fields from April 3 to June 30.
The school district charges $15 an hour for grass fields and $35 an hour for turf, and is raising those rates by roughly 50%.

budget_items.topic: Comparative cost of turf vs. town fields
budget_items.what_was_said: A summer-league high school soccer program pays about $1,500 to use the turf ten times a season, compared with Little League's roughly $2,960-$3,000 for a full spring season on town fields.

budget_items.topic: Lunenburg Youth Soccer field costs elsewhere
budget_items.what_was_said: Lunenburg Youth Soccer reportedly spends over $10,000, possibly closer to $15,000, to rent turf fields outside town.
A Groton soccer treasurer said her program pays between $13,000 and $14,000 a year across two seasons to lease fields, and that user groups there handle 100% of field maintenance themselves.
Members roughly estimated that if 800 football players split a $13,000 fee it would work out to about $16.25 per player, comparable to the town's current per-player rate.
School custodial fees for field/facility use were estimated at around $36 to $39 an hour, separate from the field rental rate itself.

decisions.decision: Continue spending down the remaining ARPA and capital funds (heard as $97,000) to finish the Marshall Park design/engineering work, without a formal vote since prior authorization already covered it.

Do not bring the Marshall Park project back to a special town meeting in November; wait roughly a year, likely spring or later, given uncertainty from the town's broader financial issues (including a tri-board group examining town finances).
Pull/rescind the prior motion granting terms to the skate park group so the agreement/extension can be revised at the next meeting.
Do not pursue the McNall or Northfield Park master plans at this time; prioritize Fitzgerald Field resurfacing on the capital planning list instead.

Chris Ruth will send the commission a list of possible capital planning items (e.g., Fitzgerald resurfacing, Powell dugouts, fencing, kayak rack) for members to review and prioritize before the next capital planning cycle.
Leave current park user fees unchanged for now; the chair will work with Angela to redesign the field reservation forms to capture actual usage before any fee changes are considered.
Reach out again to youth baseball (and others) for a breakdown of actual field usage by field and by day/hour to inform future fee decisions.
Dog-on-leash policy enforcement at McNall Park remains unresolved pending word from town counsel via the town manager on who has authority to enforce/fine violations.

Agree to let MRPC/Massachusetts Office of Outdoor Recreation document Lunenburg's parks (McNall, Fitzgerald/Ben Norman, Town Beach, Marshall Park and Pond, Wallace Park) for a statewide outdoor recreation inventory.
Tentatively keep the August 20th meeting on the calendar in case something comes up with RDLA or the town manager, even though no new information is expected by then.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission will not bring the Marshall Park project back to a town meeting vote this November, pushing it roughly a year out amid town-wide financial uncertainty.
The commission will keep spending remaining ARPA and capital funds to finish the Marshall Park design and engineering work.
The commission pulled its prior motion granting terms to the skate park group so the agreement can be revised at the next meeting.
Members left park user fees unchanged, deferring any change until reservation forms are redesigned to track actual field usage.
The commission dropped master-plan work for McNall and Northfield parks in favor of prioritizing Fitzgerald Field resurfacing on its capital list.

why_it_matters: Residents who expected a vote on Marshall Park at fall town meeting will not see one this cycle; the next opportunity is roughly a year out.

Park user fees, which members said cover only a fraction of maintenance and field costs, stay as they are for now, so any future increase will follow a usage review rather than happen at this meeting.
The skate park agreement returning to the table means its funding and construction terms are not yet final.
watch_next: Revised skate park agreement terms at the commission's next meeting
Chris Ruth's capital planning item list, to be reviewed and prioritized before the next capital planning cycle

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the big Marshall Park and capital-planning decisions, but our minutes begin mid-meeting (the entire Facilities Director and Recreation Director updates are missing) while the official minutes, in turn, omit almost every specific dollar figure discussed in the parks user-fees section that our minutes captured. The one thing a reader should check is the skate park agreement: our minutes describe the Commission pulling/rescinding the prior motion, while the official minutes say the agreement simply expired and a vote to extend it is planned for the next meeting.
